title: Tenant-aware feature flags for login policy
name: Login policy flags

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code refreshes the cached flag definitions? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The flag enforce-mfa has enabled=true, rolloutPercent=100, and tenantOverrides={"t-42": false}. What does mfaRequired return for a user in tenant t-42?
choices: True, because the global flag is enabled at 100%
False, because the tenant override is checked first and returned directly
False, but only if the user also falls into the rollout bucket
True, because overrides apply only when the flag is disabled

questions.prompt: The flag repository's database is down for several refresh cycles, so loadAll() throws. What happens in this service?
choices: The scheduler thread dies, so refreshes never run again, even after the database recovers
Every isEnabled call starts throwing the repository's exception
The failure is logged, the scheduler keeps running, and later cycles retry
The failed refresh is retried immediately in a tight loop until it succeeds

questions.prompt: enforce-mfa is at 25% rollout. For a given user in a tenant with no override, how is mfaRequired expected to behave across repeated calls and across different server instances?
choices: Randomly, with a 25% chance on each call
The same answer every time, because the bucket is derived deterministically from the flag key and user ID
The same answer on one instance but possibly different on others, because hashCode differs per JVM
The same answer until the next flag refresh, which re-randomizes buckets
